Flatten a pytree with key paths

Source: R/tree_util.R
tree_flatten_with_path.Rd

Ports of jax.tree.flatten_with_path, jax.tree.leaves_with_path and jax.tree.map_with_path (and their jax.tree_util aliases).

Usage

tree_flatten_with_path(tree, is_leaf = NULL, is_leaf_takes_path = FALSE)

tree_leaves_with_path(tree, is_leaf = NULL, is_leaf_takes_path = FALSE)

tree_map_with_path(f, tree, ..., is_leaf = NULL, is_leaf_takes_path = FALSE)

Arguments

tree

A pytree.

is_leaf

Optional predicate marking subtrees to treat as leaves.

is_leaf_takes_path

Whether is_leaf takes (path, x) instead of x.

f

Function of (path, leaf, ...) (one leaf per tree).

...

Further pytrees with the structure of tree (tree_map_with_path()).

Value

tree_flatten_with_path(): a list with leaves (a list of list(path, leaf) pairs, paths being lists of key entries) and treedef. tree_leaves_with_path(): the pairs. tree_map_with_path(): the mapped tree.

Examples

tree_leaves_with_path(list(a = 1, b = list(2, 3)))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]][[1]]
#> DictKey(key='a')
#> 
#> 
#> [[1]][[2]]
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> [[2]][[1]][[1]]
#> DictKey(key='b')
#> 
#> [[2]][[1]][[2]]
#> SequenceKey(idx=0)
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [[3]][[1]]
#> [[3]][[1]][[1]]
#> DictKey(key='b')
#> 
#> [[3]][[1]][[2]]
#> SequenceKey(idx=1)
#> 
#> 
#> [[3]][[2]]
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> 
tree_map_with_path(function(p, x) paste(keystr(p), x), list(a = 1, b = list(2, 3)))
#> $a
#> [1] "['a'] 1"
#> 
#> $b
#> $b[[1]]
#> [1] "['b'][0] 2"
#> 
#> $b[[2]]
#> [1] "['b'][1] 3"
#> 
#>
